name: DC Eats: Restaurants
subtitle: Half-Smokes, Injera & Pupusas
description:
Washington, DC's restaurants, from injera on U Street to a half-smoke all the way.

DC Eats is a free guide to eating in Washington, DC: 13 Ethiopian restaurants, 3 half-smoke counters, 2 pupuserías, 2 fish market and Wharf seafood places, a mumbo sauce carryout and a jumbo slice shop we checked by hand, plus 2,974 restaurants, cafés, bars and bakeries in 111 neighborhoods, from Georgetown and Shaw to Capitol Hill and Anacostia. No account, no ads.

WASHINGTON, DC GUIDES
• Ethiopian: injera, tibs and wat, from Shaw to Petworth.
• Half-Smokes & Chili: the District's own sausage, all the way.
• Mumbo Sauce Carryouts, Jumbo Slice and Pupuserías: wings and fries with mumbo sauce, giant slices, and Salvadoran pupusas.
• Fish Market & Wharf: crabs, fish and oysters by the water.
• MICHELIN & James Beard: the MICHELIN Guide's 20 starred restaurants, 28 Bib Gourmands and Recommended places, and James Beard honorees (118 places).
• Sidewalk Cafés & Patios: 776 places with outdoor seating on their own ABCA license.
• Oldest Places: founding years checked at the same address, oldest first.

FIND IT FAST
• Sort by distance, or browse the map by guide.
• Search by name, town, street or dish: "injera shaw", "half-smoke", "pupusas mount pleasant".
• Filter by town or cuisine, or hide chains.
• Save places, and find hand-checked places from iPhone search (Spotlight).

LIVE DETAILS FROM APPLE MAPS
Tap "Ratings, hours & photos" on any place to open Apple Maps' own place card, with current hours, photos, ratings and directions.

HOW THE LISTS ARE BUILT
Every guide place was checked by hand in fall 2026 against a 2025 or 2026 source: the place's own site or menu, dated local news, the MICHELIN Guide or its active DC business license. The rest come from Overture Maps open data, checked against the District's business licenses, plus licensed restaurants and bars the map data missed. Each place shows its own DC business and alcohol licenses. DC Health inspects pass/fail and posts no grade, so each place links DC Health's own inspection search. Website links are checked too. Nothing is ranked by star ratings, and the app computes no grades. Newer restaurant data downloads from the DC Eats website when there is some.

PRIVATE BY DESIGN
No account, no tracking, no ads. Your location, if you share it, only sorts lists on your device. Saved places stay on your device.

Places open and close, so check before you go. Spot a mistake? Email nick@eatsranked.com.

An independent app, not affiliated with any restaurant, chain or government agency (including the District of Columbia government, DC Health and the Alcoholic Beverage and Cannabis Administration), or with the MICHELIN Guide or the James Beard Foundation. MICHELIN and the MICHELIN Guide are trademarks of Michelin. James Beard Foundation and James Beard Award are trademarks of the James Beard Foundation. Place data from Overture Maps Foundation (CDLA Permissive 2.0) and others; sources and licenses are on the About tab.

reviewNotes:
1. Purpose and audience: DC Eats is a free guide to restaurants in Washington, DC (the U.S. district). Its focus is the District's own food: 13 Ethiopian restaurants, half-smoke counters, mumbo sauce carryouts, a jumbo slice shop, pupuserías and Wharf seafood, each checked by hand in fall 2026 against a 2025 or 2026 source, plus 118 MICHELIN Guide and James Beard honorees. It also lists 2,974 restaurants, cafés and bars in 111 neighborhoods from open map data, checked against the District's own business licenses. It is for residents and visitors deciding where to eat, with no ads, account or tracking.

2. How to use it (no login, no setup, no sample files needed):
- Home → Ethiopian (or Half-Smokes & Chili, Mumbo Sauce Carryouts, Jumbo Slice, Pupuserías, Fish Market & Wharf, MICHELIN & James Beard, Sidewalk Cafés & Patios, Oldest Places, Near Me) → tap any place.
- On a place, tap "Ratings, hours & photos" to open Apple Maps' own place card through MapKit. Directions, Call and Website are below it; further down are the place's DC business and alcohol licenses, and a link opens DC Health's own inspection search in Safari.
- Search from the Home search box by name, town, street or dish ("injera shaw", "half-smoke", "pupusas mount pleasant").
- The Map tab shows each guide as pins. "My location" and the Nearest sort use location only if allowed, on the device.
- The heart saves a place on the device (Saved tab). The About tab lists the sources, licenses and the independence statement.
- On iPad, a sidebar replaces the tabs; a place opens in the right-hand column.
- Location: if you're outside Washington, DC (as App Review usually is), the map says so and stays on Washington, DC, and distance sorting still works from where you are.
- "DC Eats" is the Home Screen name of "DC Eats: Restaurants".

3. External services and data:
- Apple MapKit: maps, local search to find a place's Apple Maps listing, and Apple's place card for live hours, photos and ratings.
- Core Location: optional, on-device only, for distance sorting.
- Data updates: at most once a day, the app checks the DC Eats website (static files on GitHub Pages) for newer restaurant data and downloads it if there is some. The requests carry no identifiers or location.
- No backend, accounts, analytics, advertising, payments or AI services. The restaurant data is bundled in the app.
- Bundled data sources: Overture Maps Foundation open place data (CDLA Permissive 2.0 and others; license texts are in the app); DC business licenses from Open Data DC and ABCA's current alcohol license holders (public records); MICHELIN Guide and James Beard Foundation honors (facts only); and our own research of public websites and local news. Inspection reports are not copied: each place links to DC Health's own public search.
- The website with the privacy policy and support page is static and hosted on GitHub Pages: https://nickstrom5.github.io/dc-eats/

4. Regional differences: none. The content covers Washington, DC; the app is offered in the United States and works the same everywhere.

5. Regulated or protected material: the app is not in a regulated industry and includes no protected third-party material. The data is open-licensed or public record, with attribution and licenses on the About tab. Ratings, hours and photos are shown only inside Apple's own place card through MapKit; the app stores no ratings or reviews. The app shows no inspection results and computes no grades; licenses are shown as the District records them. Every website link was checked before release, and adult venues are excluded. The app is independent and not affiliated with any restaurant, agency or the MICHELIN Guide or the James Beard Foundation.
